newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss dealers play down Yeltsin role in franc drop.
newsitem.headline: Swiss dealers play down Yeltsin role in franc drop.

text.p: Swiss currency traders played down the impact on the Swiss franc of Russian President Boris Yeltsin's apparently successful heart surgery and pointed instead to fundamental factors that are weighing on the unit.

The mark was quoted at its highest levels against the franc since March 1995 after news that Yeltsin's bypass surgery went well. It 84.10/13 Swiss centimes in afternoon dealing, up from the opening 83.70/76 but off a high at 84.18.
The dollar was at 1.2730/35 francs, up from the opening 1.2655/65 but off a high at 1.2754. This was near 21-month highs hit last week.

"He seems to have survived, but this is just a continuation of the weakness (in the franc) we have been seeing," one dealer said, calling nervousness about the Russian leader's health one factor but not the most important one in the market.

"There are some very good fundamental reasons why the Swiss franc is so weak," added a dealer at a big Swiss bank, noting the Swiss National Bank's expansive monetary policy to revive the stagnant economy and rein in the strong franc.
"We are at a level where the Swiss National Bank can sleep well at night," he said.
Traders acknowledged that Yeltsin's health was being watched closely by the market.
"It was discussed in the market this morning and generally agreed that the mark would fall if Yeltsin died," one dealer said, but he also cited fundamental reasons for the franc's decline.
